A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms and theoretical results. All 21 pages of each version, including Table 1, equations and Appendices A-D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5.pdf reports theoretical algorithms, regret bounds and proofs, including in Appendices A-D. Table 1 compares analytical guarantees; empirical outcomes discussed in the introduction are attributed to other work.

after.justification: v6.pdf retains the same theoretical content and reports no original experiments, simulations or data analyses in either the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: KL-UCB and KL-LSVI-UCB retain the same least-squares estimation, exploration bonuses and Gibbs-policy updates in Algorithms 1-2 and Sections 4-5.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios for empirical training or evaluation. Contextual bandits and MDPs remain the same theoretical problem classes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparators: Online Iterative GSHF, Two-Stage Mixed-Policy Sampling, Online Iterative M-GSHF and XPO. Neither version reports empirical baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports an experimental evaluation protocol, including data splits, empirical metrics, model configurations or training budgets.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments or empirical case studies. Appendices A-D retain the same proofs and auxiliary lemmas.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars or significance tests. The analytical high-probability guarantees are also unchanged.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries appear in either version. The analytical regret and sample-complexity bounds in Table 1 and the reported theoretical findings remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, and all derivations and proofs in Appendices A-D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same logarithmic-regret claims for online KL-regularized contextual bandits and MDPs, with the same algorithmic and decomposition contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of optimism and KL regularization, Remark 3.1's discussion of preference feedback, and the conclusion's limitation concerning additional horizon dependence are unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode, bonus definitions and analytical parameter choices are retained. Neither version adds implementation instructions, hardware specifications, runtimes or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: The renamed Zhao et al. (2025) reference retains the same authors and arXiv identifier, 2502.06051, establishing that it is the same cited work. Its use in Appendix A and the paper's research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: On page 12, the Zhao et al. (2025) title changes from 'Nearly optimal sample complexity of offline kl-regularized contextual bandits under single-policy concentrability' to 'Towards a sharp analysis of offline policy learning for f-divergence-regularized contextual bandits.' The version/date stamp is updated; body prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 and both algorithm boxes retain their formatting, captions and placement. Visual inspection confirms the same main-text and appendix layouts, with no added or removed figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The revision updates one reference title and the version/date stamp while retaining the algorithms, theoretical comparisons, complete proofs, claims and limitations. These metadata edits do not establish a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
